title: Lines Do Not Match With The Pattern Fill
content:
Lines Do Not Match With The Pattern Fill

The pattern I downloaded has a look like this.

As you see some lines does not match with the Pattern Fill.

What does this mean? What is this fill anyway?

![50237a6d90ab4671bb099e6ec1823d50](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/d94fc0a5c43b42a2b9ec4e95930f1ddd/images/50237a6d90ab4671bb099e6ec1823d50Clo3D%20-%20Fill%20And%20Lines.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi. This is happening because the Particle Distance is set too high. If you select the pattern and lower the Particle Distance from 10 to 5, the internal mesh will align perfectly with the outline.
Reply 1: I thought Particle Distance is only for 3D Screen.And It act like resolution on the 3D Screen on the Garment.High Particle Distance (High Resolution) :Low Particle Distance (Low Resolution)What is the function of Particle Distance on the 2D Screen?
Reply 2: Everything in 3D is calculated as mesh, and the 2D window simply reflects this. For a user whose goal depends mostly on visuals (e.g. for animation or high quality renders), being able to see a flatlay of the mesh can be useful for fine-tuning. (You can see the mesh of the pattern pieces when toggling on "Show Mesh".) It's also possible to select parts of the mesh from the 2D window for high precision with the Select Mesh tools, or place pins in a similar manner with the Pin tools.
Reply 3: Where to disable mesh on the 2D Screen?Currently It looks like White as on the image I shared.Then I click "2D On Screen Menu - Show Mesh" and It shows some Geometrical Shapes In The Patterns.So It looks either A) In White (Like in the image I shared)B) In Geometrical Shapes ??
Reply 4: Hi, it is not possible to "disable" the mesh. Every form in any 3D software is comprised out of mesh. Please see here the different display options, but none of them will remove that the pattern pieces consist out of mesh.
content_description: This page explains why some lines in a downloaded pattern do not align with the pattern fill and clarifies the concept of pattern fills.

title: How to hold this dress
content:
Dear Creators,

Please note I have tried to make a dress 👗, but I'm struggling to fix this point, because no shoulder joints and front and back is up and down, could anyone assist me how to fix this... I'm thinking to use attach to avatar measure tool. Is any other options to make perfect for this type of dresses. 

Thank you for your valuable time and suggestions.

Thanks ![07af91e908e94c9f976c3f912ed799a1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/4839c39deb684d5b97ca5f271e5e2ab0/images/07af91e908e94c9f976c3f912ed799a1Screenshot%202026-02-14%20131532.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Govindaraj,The issue here isn’t just about “holding” the dress, the base pattern itself needs some correction, otherwise any simulation method will keep giving problems.From what I see:The side seams between front and back don’t look consistent, which can cause that up/down shifting.The waist curves are uneven, so the garment may twist during simulation.The top area doesn’t have proper structure (neckline/shoulder shaping), so it has nothing to sit on the avatar correctly.I’d suggest fixing the pattern first before trying Attach to Avatar:Turn on symmetry and clean one side, then mirror it.Smooth out the curves and remove extra points.Make sure front and back side seam lengths match.Refine the neckline so it has proper shape and support.For simulation:Use Arrangement Points to position it properly.You can use Strengthen temporarily to stabilize.If needed, add a few Tack points instead of attaching the whole garment.Attach to Avatar can work, but it’s usually not the best approach for this type of dress.If you can share the full front and back pattern view, I can point out exactly where to adjust.

Comment 2: Hi, could you please share a screenshot of the current simulation status as well? What do you mean by no shoulder joints? We don't usually give patternmaking advice, but note that if this is (I assume) a back and a front piece, it is unlikely the garment would be made with any other fabric than one with minimum 10% elastane content (as it is lacking darts and the waist-to-hip ratio is quite small) as well as the sideseams not looking symmetrical.
content_description: A community forum page for creators to seek advice and share solutions on fixing garment fitting issues in digital dressmaking.

title: Applying Symmetry To The Patterns With The Other Has A Difference On It
content:
![f598a1427da3439487ef44007f1bfcd4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/7ef7170a2146415ab0e7dc499be5d425/images/f598a1427da3439487ef44007f1bfcd4Screenshot%202026-02-13%20at%2015.05.21.png)

Question 1) Can I grade these two Front Trousers Patterns at once while applying them symmetry?

Note that the one has Placket Place on It.

Question2 ) And I want to apply grading to the Placket Pattern and It applies to the Placket Pattern place on the trousers automatically.

Does this method alright?

I draw the placket place on the trousers then Transform Tool - Choose the placket place pattern and - Clone As Pattern

Is this differ than the method Layer Clone Under method in the way that if It makes left front trousers pattern different than the right front trousers pattern.

(So they can not be graded at once? Since they are not symmetric)

Question 2) Can I choose “Symmetrical With Sewing” for more than two patterns?

Like choosing all the patterns and apply symmetry.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi! 1. Since the front patterns don't have the exact same pattern outline, the grade rules will not be applied as no symmetry can be applied. You will have to copy and paste the rules from one point to the other. 2. Layer Clone Over/Under automatically generates a turned seamline from host piece to the cloned one, so it depends on if you want this. You can remove the seamline, though. 3. Simply try this out - it is possible.
Reply 1: New Question 1) You say you can not apply symmetry to these front patterns because the outline is not the same. Maybe the placket on the trousers is drawn with a internal polygon???Then what does happen?
Reply 2: Hi! The internal polygon will be reflected on both sides if symmetry is applied, but also, internal lines do not produce outlines, so it will not be able to function as a placket. You could sew on the placket shape as an additional pattern piece, though (and then help fake the look as a continuous piece by deleting the seamline's normal map so there is no shadow).
Reply 3: As far as I understand from your answer symmetry can be applied to these patternsA) Front Trousers Pattern B) Front Trousers Pattern With A Placket Pattern On It Drawn With "Internal Polygon" Tool.
Reply 4: Hi, CLO will not let you symmetrize the patterns if they are not identical. However, you can delete the side without the placket and make a symmetrical copy. Afterwards, cut off the placket on the side that should keep it, and delete the unnecessary extra placket on the other side. You will not be able to create a placket out of internal lines because internal lines do not produce outlines for pattern pieces.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on grading multiple garment patterns with symmetry, including handling placket placements and using cloning methods to ensure accurate and efficient pattern adjustments.

title: Change default seam allowance
content:
Hi all, I sew with 1/2 inch seam allowance. However, the default seam allowance applied in CLO3D is 1cm. I have had to reprint multiple patterns because I did not notice that the wrong seam allowance had been applied. Is there a way to change the default seam allowance from 1cm to 1/2 inch?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, unfortunately, it is not yet possible to change the seam allowance's tool default value, but it is set to be implemented in a future release.

title: CLO Looping piece through zip puller
content:
Hi there, I am trying to loop a piece of fabric (small pattern) through the end of a zip puller, I have tried pin box mesh some areas but I can't work out to actually loop the end through. Would appreciate any tips on this thanks.

![bcd57c9735614cb095869a84a4d55239](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/7ac1625e2aa449189d71d12aa5c35c31/images/bcd57c9735614cb095869a84a4d55239image.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi! The workaround suggested in the past is to make and register a zipper with the fabric attached to part of the puller. But the fabric will be solid and not drape.Or tack a pattern piece to that area so it looks "attached".
